Entries.SourceTerm: 家家門前赫日月，太平不用將軍威

Senses.PreferredTarget: Sun and moon shine before every household; in a peaceful age a general’s force is unnecessary
AlternateTargets: Each doorway has its own bright sun and moon; peace needs no show of military might
SearchAliases: sun moon shine at every door peace needs no force
every household bright light general unnecessary
Senses.Note: The first clause gives every household bright sun and moon at its own doorway. The second says that a peaceful world has no need to call on a general’s force. Chan masters use the paired image when something is already openly present and a further show of force or contrivance would add little: Shipu sets aside elaborate handling of an old case, Yikui points to the plain present matter, and Dai’an puts familiar stick-and-shout displays aside. The line’s peace is an analogy for unforced clarity, while the image retains its ordinary civic sense.

Senses.Explanation: When light is already at every door, another show of force adds little. Shipu puts aside elaborate case work, while Yikui says the plain matter is already before everyone. Both close with the paired image. Shuzhong uses it in a memorial address; Dai’an raises the whisk after setting aside familiar stick-and-shout forms. Nanshi uses the same pair after assessing old masters, ending the need for further display in his own hall.

The graph means what belongs to ordinary household usage. Buhui calls ordinary tea and rice surprising, Zhe’an calls his own calculation household-ordinary, and Shixi calls the meal celebration ordinary. Liangshan’s lamp recension uses the longer household-tea-and-rice phrase and contrasts it with another kind of speech. The records therefore use 家常 for customary fare, calculation, and occasion-specific routine; the praise or criticism belongs to each surrounding passage.

Senses.Note: Bai Ze is the lore-bearing creature whose picture identifies uncanny beings. Luopu gives the line as an answer to a question that tries to swallow the whole sea in a hair. Feiyin uses it to challenge a glib account of awakening; Yinyuan describes an empty hall where even ghosts cannot enter; Yushan brings it to the real person with no rank. The picture stands for recognition that leaves a specter no place to hide.

Senses.Note: “Without small helpers, no gentleman’s house” becomes a flexible Chan response. Guxue uses it to answer a question about descendants; Fangrong uses it when asked why wise and foolish people mingle. Yunwai makes it an answer about one who is not companion to the ten thousand things. Jiqi brings it into a warning about the thieves of the eighteen realms. The proverb points to relationships the questioner would prefer to leave out; none of these uses requires literal servants.

Senses.Note: The household and state images each connect flourishing conditions with a capable person who serves within them. Yezhu cites the pair when discussing successors; the nun Zukui Fu answers a question about a school with it. Foyuan uses it in an exchange about the inner matter, and Huanglian calls for people able to support the community. The pair praises the fit between a living tradition and people who can carry it.

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 面亦無門，古人向什麼處見客？若道得接手句，許你天上天下□顧□去。大眾，人無遠慮，必有近憂，爭如國清五峰匌帀，雙㵎蓮環，閑則遊山，渴則飲水，那裏不是見客處？又云：若道得接手句，許汝天上天下。師云：吽！吽！佛法禪道則不無，接手一句也是大斧斫三門。良久，以拄杖畫一畫，云：會麼？金地嶺胷中丘壑，赤城山皮裡陽秋，華頂峯腦門著地，桐栢觀稽首叩頭。喝一喝，下座。上堂，舉金峯和尚一日見臨濟來，乃橫按拄杖。濟拍手三下，便參堂去。峯下去，人事了，遂問：主賓相見，各有儀範。上座何得無禮？濟打一坐具。峯擬問，濟再打一坐具。峯云：山僧失利。便歸方丈。師云：一人將通草杖攬動四大海水，一人用無文印印破十方虗空。如今不得動著，動著則三一棒。參！上堂，舉：趙州遊方到臨濟，在後架洗脚次，濟見便問：如何是祖師西來意？州云：恰值老僧洗脚。濟近前作聽勢，州云□：便會去，𪅎󲣅作甚麼？濟便歸方丈。州云：三十年行脚，今日錯為人下注脚。師云：甚處是趙州錯為人下注脚處？良久，云：家貧猶自可，路貧愁殺人。上堂：雲外千峯秀，目前雙㵎清。若作如是會，永劫受沉淪。上堂，舉：瑯瑘覺和尚一日陞堂，有僧出，畫一圓相，瑘打云：道！道！僧云：不道！不道！瑘又打云：道！道！僧云：不道！不道！瑘又打云：道！道！僧云：三世諸佛不離於□。瑘又□喚維那趂出院，瑘却陞座，以手指僧云：大眾！比丘犯波逸提，山僧入地獄。師拈云：人情若好，喫水也肥。比丘犯波逸提，為甚麼瑯瑘却入地獄？良久，云：會便會去，山僧與你共證。乃合掌云：施者、受者俱獲五常色、力、命，安得無礙辯？上堂，舉：僧問雲門：如何是透法身句？門云：北斗裏藏身。師云：諸人還透得也未？傅大士云：空手把鋤頭，步行騎水牛，人從橋上過，橋流水不流。若喚作法身，入地獄如箭射；若不喚作法身，入地獄如箭射。你作麼生透？參！上堂：今朝七月初一，叢林法歲將周。便請解開布袋，相從觸處□遊。解與不解總得，而今要休便休。凡聖本無忌諱，佛魔總是冤讎。靜悄悄沒干涉，閙浩浩莫能收。東行不見西行利，一葉落知天下秋。圜悟禪師忌辰，上堂。錦江巨浪連三峽，九隴峯高接五天，中有導師口生角，眉毛落盡脚跟穿。擊得嘉州石佛眼中火出，驚回陝府鐵牛鼻孔生煙。阿呵呵！莫怨天。有利無利，不離行市；伸手縮手，無黨無偏。卓拄杖，云：釅茶三五盌，意在钁頭邊。

Senses.Explanation: A house's characteristic style is the recognizable manner displayed in its teaching, conduct, and encounter replies. Speakers ask about the style of a named teacher, monastery, inherited line, or older model; answers commonly demonstrate it rather than define it. The same expression also describes preserving, extending, or failing an inherited manner. These uses share one referent: the characteristic way associated with a teaching house.
